table.name: account
table.purpose: Bank accounts: one row per account, with its district, statement frequency, and opening date. Referenced by loans, dispositions, transactions, and payment orders.

col_001.name: account_id
col_001.description: Primary key identifying the account; referenced by loan, disp, trans, and order tables.

col_002.name: district_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to district (district.col_001), the region where the account was opened.

col_003.name: statement_frequency
col_003.description: Frequency of account statement issuance: POPLATEK MESICNE = monthly, POPLATEK TYDNE = weekly, POPLATEK PO OBRATU = after each transaction (Czech).

col_004.name: created_date
col_004.description: Date the account was opened (1993-01-01 to 1997-12-29).

table.name: card
table.purpose: Bank payment cards issued to clients (PK, card_id; each card is linked one-to-one to a disposition/owner of an account). Card types: classic, junior, gold. This is the classic Czech bank dataset (PKDD'99) card table.

col_001.name: card_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the card; unique integer identifier for each issued card.

col_002.name: disp_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to disp (disposition), identifying the client's ownership relation to an account; one-to-one, so each card belongs to exactly one client on one account.

col_003.name: type
col_003.description: Card product type: 'classic' (standard card, 659), 'junior' (card for young clients, 145), 'gold' (premium card, 88).

col_004.name: issued
col_004.description: Date the card was issued (1993-11-07 to 1998-12-29).

table.name: client
table.purpose: Persons (bank customers) of the bank; each row is one client, linked to accounts via the disposition table and located in a district. This matches the classic Czech financial dataset (PKDD'99 Berka).

col_002.name: gender
col_002.description: Client gender: M = male, F = female.

col_003.name: birth_date
col_003.description: Client date of birth (range 1911-1987, consistent with birth dates, not transaction dates).

col_004.name: district_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to district table (district.col_001), identifying the district where the client lives; lookup values are Czech district names.

table.name: disposition
table.purpose: Links bank clients to accounts, recording each client's role on the account (owner or disponent/authorized user). This is the classic bank 'disp' (disposition) relationship table: one row per client-account pairing. Evidence: 5369 rows, references to client and account, and the OWNER/DISPONENT role flag. 4500 accounts each have exactly one OWNER; 869 additional rows are DISPONENT (secondary/authorized persons).

col_001.name: disposition_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the disposition record; unique surrogate identifier (1-13690).

col_002.name: client_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to client (client.col_001), identifying the client attached to the account. One-to-one with the disposition row; also referenced by card.col_002, since a credit card is issued to a specific client on an account.

col_003.name: account_id
col_003.description: Foreign key to account (account.col_001), identifying the account the client is attached to. Many-to-one: an account can have multiple dispositions (owner plus disponent).

col_004.name: disp_type
col_004.description: Disposition type: 'OWNER' (account holder, 4500 rows, one per account) or 'DISPONENT' (authorized additional user, 869 rows).

table.name: district
table.purpose: Demographic and economic statistics for the 77 districts (okresy) of the Czech Republic; a lookup/dimension table referenced by clients, accounts and loans (Berka/PKDD'99-style financial database).

col_001.name: district_id
col_001.description: Primary key; numeric district identifier (1-77). Referenced by client, account and loan tables.

col_002.name: district_name
col_002.description: Name of the district (Czech okres), e.g. 'Benesov', 'Brno - mesto', 'Jablonec n. Nisou'. Unique per row.

col_003.name: region
col_003.description: Region of the Czech Republic the district belongs to (8 values: north/south/east/west Bohemia, north/south Moravia, Prague, central Bohemia).

col_004.name: population
col_004.description: Number of inhabitants of the district (range ~42,821 to 1,204,953; Prague is the max).

col_005.name: municipalities_under_500
col_005.description: Count of municipalities in the district with fewer than 500 inhabitants.

col_008.name: municipalities_over_10000
col_008.description: Count of municipalities with more than 10,000 inhabitants (0-5).

col_009.name: num_cities
col_009.description: Number of cities in the district (1-11).

col_010.name: urban_inhabitants_ratio
col_010.description: Share of urban inhabitants, in percent (33.9-100.0).

col_011.name: average_salary
col_011.description: Average monthly salary in the district, in CZK (range ~8,110-12,541).

col_012.name: unemployment_rate_1995
col_012.description: Unemployment rate in 1995, in percent (0.2-7.3); one null present.

col_015.name: crimes_1995
col_015.description: Number of committed crimes in 1995 (818-85,677; Prague is the outlier max).

table.name: loan
table.purpose: Bank loans granted to accounts; one row per loan contract with amount, duration, payment schedule and repayment status (PK'99-style loans table).

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Owning account; references account.col_001 (one-to-one here, i.e. each account has at most one loan in this table).

col_003.name: loan_date
col_003.description: Date the loan was granted (1993-07-05 to 1998-12-08).

col_005.name: duration_months
col_005.description: Loan duration in months; only values 12, 24, 36, 48, 60. The suggested join to district is spurious - the values are durations, not district codes.

col_006.name: monthly_payment
col_006.description: Monthly repayment amount in CZK; consistent with amount/duration (e.g. 76080/12 = 6340).

col_007.name: status
col_007.description: Loan repayment status: A = finished, paid; B = finished, not paid (defaulted); C = running, current; D = running, in arrears/debt. Exact wording is inferred from the standard PK'99 coding; the four-category contract-status reading (finished/running x good/bad) is strongly supported by the A-D distribution.

table.name: order
table.purpose: Permanent standing payment orders: recurring payments a client has instructed the bank to make from an account to an external account at another bank (PKDD'99-style 'orders' table).

col_001.name: order_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the payment order; unique integer identifier.

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Owning account the payment order is charged to; references account.col_001 (many orders per account).

col_003.name: bank
col_003.description: Two-letter code of the receiving bank (13 distinct codes, roughly uniform). Likely a Czech bank code; exact code-to-bank mapping not available, so individual codes unresolved.

col_004.name: account_number
col_004.description: Account number of the beneficiary at the receiving bank (col_003). Nearly unique per order; no join target.

col_005.name: amount
col_005.description: Debited amount per payment, in the account currency (CZK); range 1–14,882, median ~2,596.

col_006.name: k_symbol
col_006.description: Payment purpose/symbol: SIPO = household/utility payment, UVER = loan repayment, POJISTNE = insurance, LEASING = leasing payment, empty = unspecified/other.

table.name: trans
table.purpose: Bank account transactions (Berka/PKDD'99 financial dataset). One row per transaction posted to an account, with type, operation, amount, balance, and characterization fields.

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Owning account; references account.col_001 (many transactions per account).

col_004.name: type
col_004.description: Transaction type in Czech: PRIJEM = credit/income, VYDAJ = debit/expense, VYBER = cash withdrawal.

col_005.name: operation
col_005.description: Operation mode in Czech: VYBER = cash withdrawal, VKLAD = cash deposit, PREVOD NA UCET = transfer to another account, PREVOD Z UCTU = transfer from another account, VYBER KARTOU = card withdrawal. Null when only 'type' applies.

col_007.name: balance
col_007.description: Account balance after the transaction in CZK; can be negative (overdraft).

col_008.name: k_symbol
col_008.description: Transaction characterization in Czech: UROK = interest credited, SLUZBY = services/payment for statement, SIPO = household utilities, DUCHOD = pension, UVER = loan payment, SANKC. UROK = sanction interest, POJISTNE = insurance. Blank/null when not applicable.

col_009.name: bank
col_009.description: Code of the counterparty bank for interbank transfers (two-letter codes); null for non-transfer transactions.

col_010.name: account_counterparty
col_010.description: Counterparty account number for interbank transfers; null otherwise. 0 appears as a placeholder.
